Swire Shipping defines the South Pacific region as American Samoa, Fiji, French Polynesia, Guam, Kiribati, the Marshall Islands, Micronesia, Nauru, New Caledonia, Saipan, Samoa, Tonga and Vanuatu. candidates.title: Ernst Russ offloads another feeder in fleet reshuffle
candidates.excerpt: German shipowner Ernst Russ has sold another feeder containership, continuing to trim its older boxship exposure while building up its tanker and multipurpose fleet. The Frankfurt-listed company has confirmed the sale of the 2007-built, 803 teu Mirror, without disclosing the buyer and price. The vessel is expected to change hands in January 2027. The disposal follows the sales of EF Emira and EF Emma earlier this year, extending a fleet reshuffle that has seen the Hamburg-based owner move further beyond its traditional containership business. Mirror was among six feeder vessels in which Ernst Russ bought out its joint venture partners’ holdings in October last year, part of a drive to simplify the group’s ownership structure. The company has been particularly active in tankers. In September, it added another two 18,500 dwt chemical and product tanker newbuildings at China’s Wuhu Shipyard, increasing the programme to six vessels. candidates.excerpt: Stable freight flows at the Port of Gothenburg during the first three quarters of the year Cargo volumes at the Port of Gothenburg developed steadily during January–September 2026. Container volumes remained in line with the previous year, while several segments showed clear growth. New cars increased by 14 percent and energy products by 10 percent. Ro/ro traffic and rail volumes also continued to rise. In total, 698,000 TEU* were handled at the Port of Gothenburg during the first three quarters of the year, compared with 699,000 TEU during the corresponding period in 2025. Behind the largely unchanged total volume is a 2 percent increase in laden containers, while the handling of empty containers decreased by 11 percent. Put simply, on the container side, more cargo and less air has been handled compared with the same period last year. Forest products increased 11.7%, and metallic ores and metals gained 11.6%. Farm products excluding grain, and food fell 3.7%, while grain posted a rare decline at 1.4%. candidates.title: First look: CPKC earnings
candidates.excerpt: Canadian Pacific Kansas City reported a 16% increase in third-quarter core adjusted earnings per share Wednesday, as higher freight volumes and growth in grain and intermodal revenue helped offset rising fuel costs. Revenue rose to C$4.22 billion ($3.01 billion) in the three months ended Sept. 30 from $2.61 billion a year earlier, the Calgary-based company (NYSE: CP) said in earnings released after the close of markets. Core adjusted diluted earnings increased to 91 cents per share from 78 cents, while reported diluted earnings rose 3% to 74 cents from 72 cents.
